InnoVance Pharmaceuticals - Q2 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the InnoVance Pharmaceuticals Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Laura Bennett, Senior Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Laura Bennett, SVP Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss InnoVance Pharmaceuticals' financial results for the second quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Jennifer Hale, Chief Executive Officer; John Harlan, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Carlos Mendoza, Chief Medical Officer; and Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Scientific Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jennifer Hale, CEO of InnoVance Pharmaceuticals.

Jennifer Hale, CEO:
Thank you, Laura. Good morning, everyone. InnoVance delivered a strong performance in the second quarter, driven by robust uptake from our recent product launches, significant market share gains in key oncology segments, and effective execution across our commercial and operational priorities. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic initiatives, including advancing our Precision Oncology portfolio, optimizing our sales and marketing efforts, maintaining tight control over operating expenses, navigating the evolving pricing and reimbursement environment, and accelerating growth in emerging markets.

We're particularly excited about OncoVance, our lead antibody-drug conjugate, and its potential to transform outcomes in HER2-positive cancers while generating blockbuster-level revenue trajectories.

Now, I will turn the call over to John Harlan, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

John Harlan, CFO:
Thank you, Jennifer. As Jennifer mentioned, we had a solid second quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $1.65 billion, an increase of 22% compared to the same period last year. This increase was primarily driven by exceptional demand for our new oncology launches, portfolio-wide prescription growth, and expanding international contributions.

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $180 million, or $2.15 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $280 million, or $3.35 per share.

Our operating expenses were $1.28 billion, reflecting disciplined investments in R&D and commercial expansion amid topline momentum. We continue to invest heavily in R&D to support our pipeline. Our cash position remains strong at $3.2 billion.

For the full year, we are updating our guidance to $6.8 to $7.2 billion in revenue, with non-GAAP EPS of $12.50 to $13.50.

Let me unpack the key drivers starting with our new product launches and the impressive market share gains across our portfolio, which propelled our Q2 results and underpin the raised full-year outlook. We've remained intensely focused on executing our Precision Oncology 2.0 strategy, prioritizing next-generation antibody-drug conjugates like OncoVance, bispecific T-cell engagers such as Lungara, and our cell therapy platforms to seize opportunities in the over $200 billion global oncology market.

OncoVance, our flagship ADC targeting HER2-positive metastatic breast and gastric cancers, earned full FDA approval late last year after the pivotal DESTINY-Breast09 trial. Adoption has surpassed even our highest expectations. In Q2, it delivered $285 million in net product sales, reflecting 420% year-over-year growth from $55 million and a 35% sequential increase from Q1's $210 million. Year-to-date H1 sales now stand at $495 million, aligning us solidly with our $1.4 to $1.6 billion annual target.

Prescription data underscores this momentum. IQVIA NPA shows OncoVance at 18% U.S. market share in HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer on a June moving annual total basis, up dramatically from 2% at launch and gaining 4 points quarter-over-quarter. New-to-brand prescriptions surged 52% sequentially, powered by targeted KOL outreach and real-world evidence published in The Lancet Oncology, demonstrating superior progression-free survival against Roche's Kadcyla in third-line use. Monthly total prescriptions now top 45,000, with 92% new Rx compliance, thanks to 85% Medicare Part D coverage following Inflation Reduction Act discussions. Our WAC of $18,500 per vial has remained stable, with ASP erosion below 3%.

In the U.S., which drove 92% of sales, international progress is accelerating. Europe saw $22 million in Q2 ex-U.S. revenue, mainly from Germany and the UK through our AstraZeneca partnership, reaching 12% EU5 market share via HTA approvals in France and Italy. In China, our Innovent Biologics collaboration is ramping ahead of schedule post-Phase III alignment, with $50 million in expected milestones and royalties as they launch in Q3.

Turning to Lungara, our PD-1/VEGF bispecific for frontline NSCLC, U.S. launch followed ORIENT-31 superiority results in May. It generated $62 million in six weeks, with 28,000 new Rx and 9% share in the PD-(L)1 plus VEGF category, challenging Merck's Keytruda/Avastin standard. Our ComboForge linker technology supports fixed-dose combinations, showing 15% superior durability early on.

Portfolio-wide, our oncology share hit 14.2% in U.S. targeted solid tumors per June IQVIA MAT, up 320 basis points year-over-year, outgrowing the category's 8%. Despite biosimilar pressure on Roche's Herceptin at 25% penetration, we're displacing older ADCs like Adcetris through our sBLA.

We've allocated $450 million YTD to our Singapore CMC facility, achieving 99.5% on-time fills and capacity for 150,000 patients by 2026. The FDA breakthrough-designated AI Predictive Response platform, using NGS biomarkers to spot 20% more responders, is now in OncoVance labeling.

These launches affirm our M&A approach—the $2.8 billion TrioBio deal added three late-stage assets—with OncoVance eyeing $4-5 billion peak sales by 2030 and Lungara $2.5 billion. CMS ASP tweaks and assistance programs covering 40% out-of-pocket costs counter IRA pressures. We see Q3 OncoVance at $350-380 million, Lungara at $120 million, plus Phase IIb CAR-T data at ESMO in September.

Next, on marketing and sales effectiveness metrics, which continue fueling our outperformance. Our commercial operations target total Rx and new Rx acceleration for flagships like OncoVance, Lungara, and emerging assets. Total commercial revenues rose 28% year-over-year to contribute meaningfully to our $2.4 billion quarterly topline equivalent, with marketing and sales expenses up just 12% to $450 million—for a leading 5.3x efficiency ratio, surpassing Eli Lilly's 4.8x and Novo Nordisk's 4.2x.

In prescription dynamics, U.S. operations—65% of ex-U.S. sales—saw OncoVance TRx up 15% to 4.2 million scripts at 22% GLP-1 analogous class share, from 18% last year. NRx grew 32% to 1.8 million, via 25% detailing lift. Our 3,200 reps averaged 14.2 daily scripts, beating Pfizer's 13.1, thanks to AI-optimized Veeva CRM prioritizing prescribers and lifting virtual close rates 18%.

Europe delivered 22% TRx growth to 1.1 million for key assets despite AMNOG and French delays, gaining 4 EU5 share points to 19% through omnichannel KOL tactics—40% UK NRx ramp post-NICE, 2x Italy acceleration. Asia-Pacific, 12% of sales, hit 35% TRx growth for OncoVance to 650,000 scripts, China at 60% via Sinopharm; Japan trailed at 8% pending NHI tweaks.

ROI-wise, 45% digital spend shift yielded 4.8:1 returns, topping AstraZeneca's 3.9:1. PharmaPulse AI integrates IQVIA Xponent and Komodo data for personalized HCP emails to 150,000, with 28% opens and 9% clicks—double industry norms. Patient apps like MyOncoVance enrolled 2.5 million, lifting 12-month persistence to 72% vs. 55% class average, cutting washouts 14% and adding $180 million retained revenue.

Sales force share of voice among top oncologists reached 34% from 29% per 15,000-HCP panels. Rep compliance over 95%, peer-to-peer with 120 KOLs upped NSCLC conversions 22%. VR training cut new-hire ramps 30% to 60 days, supporting 15% headcount growth for 2025 launches.

This Precision Commercialization—real-world data plus omnichannel—beats 7-9% market CAGR. Payer step edits cost 2 NRx points, biosimilars erode TNFs at 15% quarterly, but $50 million in value-based contracts cover 40% lives. Q4 TRx growth eyed at 20-25%, ROI 4.5x+, backing FY24 $9.8-10.2 billion revenue conviction.

Shifting to operating expense analysis, our total OpEx hit $1.28 billion, up 12% YoY but flat sequentially, at 78% of revenue—300 bps better than prior 81%, leveraging oncology and rare disease growth.

R&D at $892 million (70% OpEx) rose 15% YoY from $775 million, fueled by Phase 3 for next-gen bispecifics like our HER2 analog BNT-347, echoing Enhertu success. NOVEL-3 dosed first patients Q1 across 150 sites, hiking recruitment via IQVIA/PPD. Gene therapy AAV for SMA-like indications took $215 million, with NC GMP scaling and Lonza outsourcing adding 8% delta.

Efficiency shone: 5% R&D savings via BioNova Discovery Engine with NVIDIA/Insilico, slashing screening 30% and $12 million QoQ. R&D headcount up 4% to 1,850, emphasizing computational roles.

SG&A at $388 million rose 5% YoY, down 2% QoQ—30% OpEx. Post-2023 restructuring saved $45 million annualized. U.S. commercial up 7% to $185 million for PARP competitor Zynova vs. Lynparza, adding 120 reps. U.S. SG&A +10% on DTC and IRA defenses, net prices at 82% WAC. EU flat at €95 million via Vifor synergies post-EMA. Asia +3% to $45 million for Japan Sakigake with Takeda.

Excluding $18 million acquisition costs from CRISPR spinout, adjusted SG&A +2% YoY. Field medical steady at 350 for Zynova RWE, driving 22% script share.

Pipeline velocity prioritizes $2B+ peak assets like ADCs/bispecifics. CRO milestone deals with WuXi/Samsung deferred $30 million capex. OpEx/revenue to 70% year-end vs. peer 75%, Regeneron-style.

Q3 OpEx $1.25-1.35 billion, R&D flat-up 5%, SG&A efficiencies from digital cuts. FY $5.1-5.3 billion, 8-10% growth, 200bps margins.

On the pricing and reimbursement landscape, we've strengthened financial resilience. Q3 blended net realization improved 2% QoQ despite comps.

U.S. (62% revenue): IRA shadows, but no in-lines hit initial negotiations like Mounjaro/Keytruda analogs. Modeling 15-25 bps Medicare erosion 2026. Gross-to-net to 28% from 31%, disciplined rebates. ONCO-101 PD-1 WAC $185,000/course, net $142,000 at 23% rebates to CVS/Express. Foundation aid for 12,000 patients sustained 85% adherence. 340B at 42% volume via carve-outs.

Europe/ex-U.S. (28%): EU5 ORP for gene therapies in 4/5 markets fast. UK NICE Innovative Fund ICER £28,000/QALY on REACH-SMA RWE (37% ventilation drop). Germany IQWiG major benefit for ONCO-101, +4% AMNOG to €142,000. Biosimilars like Riabni/Retacrit at 22% ritux share, BIOHER-2 -8% EU QoQ; Italy VBP pilots tie 15% revenue to PFS, +€45 million.

Emerging: Japan PMDA premium JPY 320M/dose for gene therapy, 90-day chuikyo. China NRDL 19% discount offset 2.5x volume for ONCO-101.

Ahead: RWE 15 pubs incl. NEJM Evidence; OBAs refund 20% if <12-month OS; $150M patent extensions, ONCO-202 Phase 3 $2.2B peak. FY24 3-5% erosion offset by volumes; ASP +1.2% YoY, 8-10% CAGR.

Finally, geographic revenue breakdown: Q2 net sales $2.8 billion adjusted base, +18% reported/+20% FX-neutral, from oncology/immunology/rare diseases like PD-1 Aethervumab analog and CAR-T CelluMax.

U.S. 52% or $1.46B +12% YoY: Aethervumab +2.2 NSCLC share, AdaPure 85% payer penetration. IRA Part D -150 bps, offset by 65/35 commercial/gov mix.

Europe 28% $784M flat CC: 8-10% HTA cuts offset 15% HemoForge volumes; Stelara biosimilar delay resolved Q4.

ROW 20% $560M +35%/+42% CC: Japan/Australia +22% on expansions/J-codes.

Emerging markets—12% $336M +52% YoY, beating 40-45% guide, per Access 2030.

China 5% $140M +65%: Aethervumab 18% NRDL melanoma share, WuXi CDMO -22% COGS; AethBispec Phase III China-first.

India 3% $84M +48%: AdaPure 30% RA/PsA share, Hyderabad 90% util sub-Rs500/vial, PAPs 75% persistence.

LatAm 2.5% $70M +42%: Brazil CelluMax $25M compassionate, MS tenders $18M; flat ASPs hedged.

Other EM 1.5% $42M +35%: Indonesia Jak2.

EMs 25% ex-U.S. growth via regulatory (14 approvals), supply ($300M facilities -40% leads), tiered pricing (35-50% U.S. ASP), PAPs 40%, 20% pipeline EM-optimized. FY24 EM 45-50% to $1.5B/15% total; 70% FX hedge.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Carlos Mendoza, our Chief Medical Officer, to discuss our clinical programs.

Dr. Carlos Mendoza, Chief Medical Officer:
Thank you, John. We are very pleased with the progress of our clinical trials. Specifically, enrollment in the NOVEL-3 Phase 3 for our HER2 bispecific is accelerating across global sites, while our AAV gene therapy for SMA analogs advances manufacturing scale-up. Our next-gen CAR-T for solid tumors nears Phase IIb readout at ESMO, and ONCO-202 bispecific enters Phase 3 with promising early safety. We're on track for multiple milestones, including China-aligned Phase IIIs and FDA filings by year-end.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Jennifer.

Jennifer Hale, CEO:
Thank you, Carlos. We will now open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, instructions for the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Terence Mills with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Terence Mills, Bank of America:
Thanks, good morning all. Jennifer, congrats on the quarter. On OncoVance, the uptake is impressive—can you elaborate on Q3 trajectory and any supply constraints?

Jennifer Hale, CEO:
Thanks, Terence. John covered the $350-380 million Q3 guide, driven by continued NRx momentum and international ramps. Supply is rock-solid at 99.5% fill rates from Singapore, with capacity scaling fast. Our AI biomarkers are expanding the label, so we're confident.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Rachel Kim, JPMorgan:
Hi team, strong margins here. John, how should we think about OpEx progression into H2, especially R&D ramps?

John Harlan, CFO:
Good question, Rachel. Q3 at $1.25-1.35 billion as guided, with R&D flat-to-up 5% on trials but SG&A efficiencies from digital tools saving 15% travel. FY at $5.1-5.3 billion implies 200 bps margin expansion, prioritizing high-ROI like ADCs. We're ahead of peers on productivity.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Patel with Leerink Partners. Please go ahead.

David Patel, Leerink Partners:
Thanks. Carlos, on the CAR-T Phase IIb and gene therapies—what are key data expectations at ESMO and beyond?

Dr. Carlos Mendoza, Chief Medical Officer:
David, thanks. ESMO will feature solid tumor CAR-T efficacy with superior response rates versus standards, plus durability insights. Gene therapies show enhanced CNS penetration in preclinicals, aligning with SMA-like registries. Multiple readouts H2 position us for 2025 filings.

Operator:
Our next question is from Lisa Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen, Goldman Sachs:
Hi, great results. John, emerging markets growth is standout—any updates on China/India risks like pricing or regs?

John Harlan, CFO:
Lisa, EMs on track for 45-50% FY growth to 15% total revenue. China NRDL volumes offset discounts, India biosimilars navigated via local mfg. 70% FX hedge, robust moats from tailored pipeline like HCC ADCs. Access 2030 delivering.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time.

Jennifer Hale, CEO:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Laura Bennett, SVP Investor Relations:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the InnoVance Pharmaceuticals Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
